page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7t.6xlarge is a memory-optimized instance belonging to the Enhanced r7t family. Built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled. The instance integrates 192.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB allocated per thread. CPU cache resources include 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by vector extension support including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI alongside hardware cryptographic features like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage devices, requiring all persistent storage and operating system images to rely on external network-attached volumes. Networking capabilities provide a baseline throughput of 12 Gbps, while complimentary public IPv4 addresses are omitted by default.

Benchmark evaluations position the ecs.r7t.6xlarge within mid-tier performance across synthetic compute and system operations. General compute testing reports a PassMark CPU score of 29,448.33, with stress-ng recording 1,891.59 for single-core and 23,333.96 for multi-core throughput. Geekbench scoring aligns with this baseline, registering 1,586.0 for single-core and 11,631.0 for multi-core tests. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 131.14 GB/sec, while write operations sustain 64.78 GB/sec. Application testing displays 23.59 million operations per second in Redis SET routines and 28.2 GB/sec in static web serving. Small-model LLM generation reaches 302.83 tokens/sec, placing in the upper performance tier, whereas medium-model generation holds at 15.35 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency and architectural standpoint, the instance balances a significant 192 GB RAM pool against 24 dedicated compute cores without incurring the overhead of local NVMe hardware or discrete accelerator chips. This structure yields optimal efficiency for in-memory databases, large caching layers, data processing pipelines, and enterprise enterprise resource planning workloads that demand high memory capacity per core without relying on local disks.
